messages:
Maria Gomez: Heads up — got a perf profiling snapshot from prod that shows a steady allocation spike after the kernel-selector tweak yesterday. Peak working set jumps ~2.8x for long-context chat sessions.
Maria Gomez: KV cache holding large prefixes for ~120s, combined with workspace sizing increase, looks like fragmentation + no buffer reuse path on that kernel.
Maria Gomez: Opening this thread to coordinate a short mitigation playbook: (1) immediate request shaping for long seqs, (2) enable per-tenant circuit breaker, (3) temporary route to low-mem model variant, (4) force KV prefix eviction TTL to 30s. Thoughts? @Chen @Ryan
Chen Li: ack. can you paste the top lines of the perf dump?
Maria Gomez: Sure — pasted below. This is the allocation timeline around the spike: 
```
[2024-06-15T14:08:12Z] kernel_selector: switched to fused-attn-v2
[2024-06-15T14:08:12Z] allocator: workspace_size went from 1.2GB -> 3.1GB
[2024-06-15T14:08:13Z] kvcache: prefix_count=812, avg_prefix_bytes=2432
[2024-06-15T14:08:13Z] gpu_mem: fragmentation=0.36, largest_free_block=128MB
[2024-06-15T14:08:14Z] oom_warning: slow_allocations > 50ms
```
Chen Li: hump — fused-attn-v2 has higher peak working set for long kv cache paths. Two immediate knobs: reduce per-request workspace_max and enable soft-reserve reclaim.
Jorge Alvarez: +1 on soft-reserve. Also we should gate the selector so long-seq requests pick the older kernel until we fix buffer reuse.
Ryan Patel: I'll open a short-lived circuit breaker rule on the routing layer to reject requests with seq_len > 1024 at p99. We can return HTTP 429 + small summary so clients can retry with chunked prompts.
Maria Gomez: Suggested quick config snippet for ops to apply (can run via deploy script): 
```json
{
  "circuit_breakers": [
    {"name": "long_seq_shed", "cond": "seq_len > 1024", "action": "reject", "status": 429, "window_s": 60}
  ],
  "kvcache": {"prefix_ttl_s": 30, "eviction_mode": "aggressive"},
  "allocator": {"workspace_max_mb": 1024, "enable_soft_reserve": true}
}
```
Chen Li: Nice. Also toggle kernel selector cooldown: map long-seq to fused-attn-v1 variant. We have a routing policy that can override kernel_variant per-request.
Maria Gomez: ops-bot — create incident and run canary with these mitigations?
ops-bot: Incident #INC-20240615-71 created by Maria Gomez. Runbook tag: allocation-shepherd. Assigned: eng-runtime oncall.
Ryan Patel: Canary steps I will run: (1) enable circuit breaker via ctrlapi, (2) set kvcache.prefix_ttl to 30s on a subset of nodes, (3) flip selector map for tenant:plg-canary to fused-attn-v1, (4) observe p50/p95/p99 memory and slow_allocations metric for 15m.
Jorge Alvarez: Metric names to watch: runtime.alloc_peak_bytes, runtime.fragmentation_ratio, kvcache.prefix_count, slow_allocations_ratio. Also add alert if alloc_peak > 2GB for canary nodes.
Chen Li: If canary looks good, plan a staged rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 100% traffic, 15m steady windows. Also schedule a follow-up: rework buffer reuse path for fused-attn-v2 (ticket INF-4921).
Maria Gomez: Thanks — I'll file INF-4921 with profiling artifacts, and add the playbook steps to the incident. Quick mitigation checklist in order: 
- apply circuit breaker rule (Ryan)
- reduce workspace_max to 1GB (ops)
- set kvcache.prefix_ttl=30s for affected nodes (Ryan)
- override kernel selector mapping for long-seq to v1 (Chen)
- start canary, monitor metrics (All)
- if regressions continue -> route to dedicated low-mem pool (fallback)
Ryan Patel: Will run the ctrlapi commands now. Pasting sample: 
```bash
# enable circuit breaker
curl -X POST $CTRLAPI/routing/circuit_breakers -d '@cb.json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
# set kvcache ttl
curl -X PATCH $CTRLAPI/nodes/affected -d '{"kvcache": {"prefix_ttl_s":30}}'
```
Maria Gomez: Also note for postmortem: add kernel selection perf test for long seqs to CI with kv cache enabled — prevents regressions.
Jorge Alvarez: one more: consider increasing background eviction frequency temporarily to reduce fragmentation. set kvcache.eviction_interval_s=10.
Chen Li: Good call. I'll own the follow-up kernel revert PR if needed.
Maria Gomez: Great team. I'll update INC-20240615-71 with the checklist and close this slack thread once canary passes. :thumbsup:
